title: Recovery — Mobility Flow
subtitle: Full-body mobility, no equipment
coaching_note: This is still training — treat it like a session, not a rest day extra. Move slow, breathe deep, and don't rush through tight spots to get to the end.

phases.name: Lower Body Mobility
phases.coaching_note: Move slow and controlled — this is about range of motion, not a workout pace.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Big step into a lunge, drop the back knee, plant the same-side hand down, rotate your other arm up toward the ceiling.
exercises.why: One move that opens the hip flexor, hamstring, and thoracic spine together — the most efficient mobility drill there is.

exercises.name: 90-90 Hip Switch
exercises.form_cue: Seated, both knees bent at 90 degrees, one in front and one to the side. Rotate through to switch which leg is in front, keeping your chest tall.
exercises.why: Trains internal and external hip rotation — range most people lose sitting all day and never get back.

exercises.name: Deep Squat Hold
exercises.form_cue: Feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, sink as deep as you can with heels down. Hold a doorframe if you need balance.
exercises.why: The deep squat position is a compressed test of ankle, knee, and hip mobility all at once.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Heel down, toes up against a wall for the straight-knee version, then a slight bend for the soleus.
exercises.why: Tight calves limit ankle range, which quietly loads the knee and hip on every step.

exercises.name: Thoracic Rotation (quadruped)
exercises.form_cue: On all fours, one hand behind your head, rotate your elbow up toward the ceiling following it with your eyes, then thread it back under.
exercises.why: Directly targets thoracic rotation — the piece most people are missing that forces the lower back to compensate.

exercises.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Forearm on the doorframe, elbow at shoulder height, gently lean your body through the door.
exercises.why: Opens the chest and front of the shoulder — the muscles that pull posture forward all day at a desk.

exercises.name: Neck Circles
exercises.form_cue: Slow and gentle, small range. Stop anywhere that pinches.
exercises.why: Releases neck tension that builds up from screen time and stress, easy to skip but worth the minute.

exercises.name: Box Breathing
exercises.form_cue: Inhale 4 counts, hold 4, exhale 4, hold 4. Repeat for the full three minutes.
exercises.why: Downshifts your nervous system — the actual point of a recovery day is recovery, not just stretching.

progression_notes: If any joint feels consistently restricted week over week, flag it — that's worth a closer look rather than just more stretching.
